title: Data Structures: Lists & Maps
description: Learn how to store and organize collections of data using lists, maps, and sets.

concepts.example_text: Individual variables work for single values, but real programs deal with groups of data — a list of users, a shopping cart of items, a dictionary of word definitions. Collections let you store, access, and manipulate groups of related values efficiently.

Lists use zero-based indexing. The first element is at index 0, the second at index 1, etc. In the list ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], 'apple' is at index 0 and 'cherry' is at index 2. Accessing an index that doesn't exist causes a runtime error.

Use a List when order matters and you access by position (a playlist). Use a Map when you need key-value lookups (a phone book — name → number). Use a Set when you need unique values with no duplicates (a collection of unique tags).

terms.definition: An ordered collection of elements, accessed by index. Elements can be repeated. Most fundamental collection type.
A collection of key-value pairs. Each key is unique and maps to a value. Used for lookups and structured data.
An unordered collection of unique elements. Adding a duplicate is silently ignored. Useful for membership testing.
The numerical position of an element in a list. Typically starts at 0 (zero-based indexing).
The process of going through each element in a collection one at a time, typically using a for or for-in loop.

questions.question: What index does the first element of a list have?
questions.explanation: In almost all modern programming languages, lists/arrays use zero-based indexing. The first element is at index 0.

questions.question: Which data structure uses key-value pairs?
questions.explanation: A Map (also called Dictionary or Object) stores data as key-value pairs, like a phonebook mapping names to phone numbers.

questions.question: What happens when you add a duplicate value to a Set?
questions.explanation: Sets only contain unique values. Adding a value that already exists is silently ignored — no error, but no duplicate is created.

questions.question: Which collection should you use to store a ranked leaderboard?
questions.explanation: A List preserves order, making it ideal for ranked data like leaderboards where position (1st, 2nd, 3rd) matters.

questions.question: What does list.length return for ['a', 'b', 'c']?
questions.explanation: The length property returns the number of elements in the list. ['a', 'b', 'c'] has 3 elements, so length is 3. Note: the last index is length - 1 = 2.
